Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0007] Reuse existing period-arithmetic helpers and conventions: Before implementing a new date/period function, read sibling modules for established helpers and error conventions and mirror them.
  Inspect related modules (e.g. subscriptions.py, clock.py, errors.py) first: reuse ensure_utc for timezone normalization and BillingError with a short code for invalid input, so the new function behaves consistently with the rest of the library.
- [rb-0008] Compute strictly-after renewal with floor division plus one: For periodic events anchored at a start time, the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp is start + ((after - start) // length + 1) * length.
  Handle the before-start case separately (return start + length, since the start itself is not a renewal), then use integer floor division on timedeltas to get the index and add one. This avoids off-by-one errors when `after` lands exactly on a renewal.
- [rb-0006] Inspect models and tests before implementing: Reading dataclass definitions and existing tests up front clarifies field names, defaults, and expected return semantics, reducing rework.
  Before writing code, cat models.py, errors.py, and relevant tests to confirm constructor signatures (e.g. LineItem(description, quantity, unit_price)) and how the function will be called. This avoids mismatched argument order or wrong status field names.
- [rb-0011] Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits: Finance policy requires a second approver for support-initiated refunds above 500.00 via keyword-only approved_by=None.
  After normalizing the amount, raise BillingError("approval_required") when amount > 500.00 and approved_by is falsy; amounts at or below the threshold need no approval. Keep the parameter keyword-only so existing callers are unaffected.
- [rb-0009] Validate period_days defensively, excluding bool: Guard against non-positive or non-integer period_days, remembering that bool is a subclass of int in Python.
  Check `isinstance(period_days, int) and not isinstance(period_days, bool) and period_days > 0` before building the timedelta, raising BillingError('invalid_period', ...) otherwise; this prevents zero-division and silently wrong schedules.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and coercion: When implementing monetary functions, inspect the repo's money module and reuse its to_money/round_money helpers instead of ad-hoc round().
  Search for existing helpers (e.g. ledgerly/money.py) before writing arithmetic. Using to_money for input coercion and round_money for output ensures consistent cent rounding and Decimal handling that hidden tests likely expect.
